Carson's setup (2026-09-14): **all code edits happen in this Windows `Gitea` folder** (logged
SpecStory sessions launch here). WSL Debian `~/gitea` is a **test runner only** — never edit there.
Native Windows test runs produce Windows-only failures, and lint is ~20x slower, so don't trust them.

**Run tests/lint/build with `wsync` from the Bash tool (Git Bash):**
```bash
wsync pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/features/common-page.test.ts
wsync go test -run '^TestName$' ./routers/web/misc/
wsync make lint-js
wsync make build
wsync            # sync only
```
`C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync` reads the branch checked out here, warns if tracked files are
uncommitted (only COMMITTED work reaches WSL — commit first, ask Carson before committing), then
runs WSL `~/bin/wsync-wsl <branch> [cmd]`: fetches remote `win` (this folder over /mnt/c;
push disabled), force-switches `~/gitea` to that branch, runs the command with Go 1.26.4/Node PATH.

Gotchas: don't run `git status` on `/mnt/c` from WSL (hangs); WSL can't run `.exe`s; use
`wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c '...' name args` (plain `wsl -- bash -c` drops args).
To try the app: `~/gitea/custom/conf/app.ini` serves Gitea on http://localhost:3001 (SQLite) —
run `wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea web'` in the background after `wsync make build`.
Baseline rule: some backend tests fail on `main` too — compare branch vs `main`, not vs zero.

name: gitea-toolchain-setup
description: Toolchain for the CSCI 435 Gitea project — pinned Go version, make-from-Git-Bash rule, stale corepack step
metadata:
  type: project
---

Installed 2026-09-02 for [[csci-435-gitea-project]]: **Go 1.26.4**, Node 26.7.0, corepack 0.36.0,
pnpm 11.9.0, GNU Make 4.4.1 (ezwinports, at
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Packages\ezwinports.make_*\bin`). No gcc needed (pure-Go SQLite,
`CGO_ENABLED=0`). Verified: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `vite build`, `go build` (~149 MB
`gitea.exe`), and `make fmt` all exit 0 with a clean tree.

**Go must stay on 1.26.x — do not upgrade to 1.27.** `go.mod` says `go 1.26.4` and CI resolves from
it (`go-version-file: go.mod`). Go 1.27's gofmt reformats multi-value composite-literal returns, so
`make fmt` under 1.27 rewrites `modules/git/key.go` and drags unrelated churn into PRs. Confirmed by
testing both versions. The winget package is **pinned** (`winget pin add --id GoLang.Go`), so
`winget upgrade --all` skips it; `winget pin remove --id GoLang.Go` if the course bumps `go.mod`.

**Run `make` from Git Bash, never PowerShell.** PowerShell has no POSIX `sh` on PATH, so make falls
back to `cmd.exe` and dies with `'sed' is not recognized`. Do NOT "fix" this by adding Git's
`usr\bin` to the global PATH — it shadows Windows `find`/`sort`.

**`STUDENTS.md` is stale on pnpm:** it says `corepack enable`, but Node 25+ unbundled corepack, so
that fails on Node 26. Fix used: `npm install -g corepack@latest`, then `corepack enable pnpm` and
`corepack prepare pnpm@11.9.0 --activate`. npm's global prefix is user-writable (no admin), but Go
and Node MSIs raise UAC prompts Claude cannot click — Carson must approve those.

Tests: do not run on native Windows (`STUDENTS.md` — symlink/temp-file failures that aren't real
bugs). WSL2 Debian is now set up — run tests via `wsync <cmd>`, see [[gitea-wsync-test-workflow]].

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# WSL side of wsync: sync ~/gitea (test runner only) to a branch from the Windows Gitea folder, then run a command.
# Called from Windows Git Bash as: wsync [command...]   (see C:\Users\carso\bin\wsync)
# Usage here: wsync-wsl <branch> [command...]
set -e
export PATH="$HOME/.local/go/bin:$HOME/.local/node/bin:$HOME/go/bin:$PATH"
branch="$1"; shift
cd ~/gitea
if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: ~/gitea has local edits (it should never be edited). Inspect with: git -C ~/gitea status"; exit 1
fi
git fetch -q win
git switch -q -C "$branch" "win/$branch"
echo "WSL ~/gitea now at $branch: $(git log --oneline -1)"
if [ $# -gt 0 ]; then echo "+ $*"; "$@"; fi

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package issues
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"slices"
+	"strings"
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"gitea.dev/modules/util"
+)
+
+// CloseReason records why an issue or pull request was closed.
+// It is stored as an integer, so existing values must never be renumbered.
+type CloseReason int
+
+const (
+	CloseReasonNone       CloseReason = iota // 0
+	CloseReasonCompleted                     // 1
+	CloseReasonNotPlanned                    // 2
+	CloseReasonDuplicate                     // 3
+	CloseReasonOther                         // 4
+)
+
+// CloseReasonUnknown is never stored: it stands for an unrecognised reason name, so that Validate rejects it.
+const CloseReasonUnknown CloseReason = -1
+
+// CloseReasonTextMaxLength matches the VARCHAR(255) close_reason_text column and the close form's MaxSize(255)
+// rule. Validate counts characters the same way MaxSize does, so paths that skip the form get the same limit.
+// MSSQL's NVARCHAR counts UTF-16 units instead, so text with many emoji can pass this limit and still not fit.
+const CloseReasonTextMaxLength = 255
+
+// AllowedCloseReasons lists the reasons a person can pick when closing.
+// A pull request is completed by merging, so it cannot be closed as completed.
+func AllowedCloseReasons(isPull bool) []CloseReason {
+	if isPull {
+		return []CloseReason{CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
+	}
+	return []CloseReason{CloseReasonCompleted, CloseReasonNotPlanned, CloseReasonDuplicate, CloseReasonOther}
+}
+
+// CloseReasonOptions is the reason a person gives when closing an issue or pull request.
+type CloseReasonOptions struct {
+	Reason         CloseReason
+	Text           string // only for CloseReasonOther
+	DuplicateIndex int64  // only for CloseReasonDuplicate: the number of the issue it duplicates, in the same repository
+}
+
+// Validate checks the options for an issue or pull request, without looking anything up;
+// SetIssueAsClosed checks that the duplicate target exists.
+// No reason at all is valid, so close paths that give none keep working.
+func (opts CloseReasonOptions) Validate(isPull bool) error {
+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonNone && !slices.Contains(AllowedCloseReasons(isPull), opts.Reason) {
+		return ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed{Reason: opts.Reason, IsPull: isPull}
+	}
+
+	if opts.Reason == CloseReasonDuplicate {
+		if opts.DuplicateIndex <= 0 {
+			return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "no issue number given"}
+		}
+	} else if opts.DuplicateIndex != 0 {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate{Index: opts.DuplicateIndex, Detail: "an issue number is only allowed with the duplicate reason"}
+	}
+
+	hasText := strings.TrimSpace(opts.Text) != "" // whitespace-only counts as no text
+	if opts.Reason != CloseReasonOther {
+		if hasText {
+			return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is only allowed with the other reason"}
+		}
+		return nil
+	}
+	if !hasText {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: "text is empty"}
+	}
+	if utf8.RuneCountInString(opts.Text) > CloseReasonTextMaxLength {
+		return ErrInvalidCloseReasonText{Reason: opts.Reason, Detail: fmt.Sprintf("text is longer than %d characters", CloseReasonTextMaxLength)}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed represents a reason that is out of range, or not allowed for the issue or pull request.
+type ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed struct {
+	Reason CloseReason
+	IsPull bool
+}
+
+// IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed checks if an error is a ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed.
+func IsErrCloseReasonNotAllowed(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("close reason is not allowed for this %s [reason: %d]", util.Iif(err.IsPull, "pull request", "issue"), err.Reason)
+}
+
+func (err ErrCloseReasonNotAllowed) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}
+
+// ErrInvalidCloseReasonText represents close reason text that is empty, too long, or sent with a reason other than CloseReasonOther.
+type ErrInvalidCloseReasonText struct {
+	Reason CloseReason
+	Detail string
+}
+
+// IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseReasonText.
+func IsErrInvalidCloseReasonText(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseReasonText)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid close reason text: %s [reason: %d]", err.Detail, err.Reason)
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseReasonText) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}
+
+// ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate represents a duplicate target that is missing, is the issue itself, or is not in the same repository.
+type ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate struct {
+	Index  int64
+	Detail string
+}
+
+// IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate checks if an error is a ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate.
+func IsErrInvalidCloseDuplicate(err error) bool {
+	_, ok := err.(ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate)
+	return ok
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Error() string {
+	return fmt.Sprintf("invalid duplicate target: %s [index: %d]", err.Detail, err.Index)
+}
+
+func (err ErrInvalidCloseDuplicate) Unwrap() error {
+	return util.ErrInvalidArgument
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.

+
+package v1_27
+
+import (
+	"gitea.dev/models/db"
+
+	"xorm.io/xorm"
+)
+
+func AddCloseReasonToIssue(x db.EngineMigration) error {
+	type Issue struct {
+		CloseReason           int    `xorm:"SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"`
+		CloseReasonText       string `xorm:"VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT ''"`
+		CloseDuplicateIssueID int64  `xorm:"NOT NULL DEFAULT 0"`
+	}
+	_, err := x.SyncWithOptions(xorm.SyncOptions{
+		IgnoreDropIndices: true,
+		IgnoreConstrains:  true,
+	}, new(Issue))
+	return err
+}

+// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+package v1_27
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+
+	"gitea.dev/models/migrations/migrationtest"
+
+	_ "gitea.dev/models/issues" // registers the issue table; fixtures for unregistered tables are skipped
+
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
+	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
+)
+
+func Test_AddCloseReasonToIssue(t *testing.T) {
+	type Issue struct {
+		ID       int64 `xorm:"pk autoincr"`
+		RepoID   int64 `xorm:"INDEX UNIQUE(repo_index)"`
+		Index    int64 `xorm:"UNIQUE(repo_index)"`
+		IsClosed bool  `xorm:"INDEX"`
+		IsPull   bool  `xorm:"INDEX"`
+	}
+
+	x, deferable := migrationtest.PrepareTestEnv(t, 0, new(Issue))
+	defer deferable()
+
+	require.NoError(t, AddCloseReasonToIssue(x))
+
+	var issues []struct {
+		ID                    int64
+		CloseReason           int
+		CloseReasonText       string
+		CloseDuplicateIssueID int64
+	}
+	require.NoError(t, x.Table("issue").Asc("id").Find(&issues))
+	require.Len(t, issues, 4) // guards against the fixtures silently not loading
+	for _, issue := range issues {
+		assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseReason, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+		assert.Empty(t, issue.CloseReasonText, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+		assert.Zero(t, issue.CloseDuplicateIssueID, "issue %d", issue.ID)
+	}
+}

+func (f *CreateCommentForm) CloseReasonOptions() issues_model.CloseReasonOptions {
+	opts := issues_model.CloseReasonOptions{Text: f.CloseReasonText, DuplicateIndex: f.CloseDuplicateIndex}
+	switch f.CloseReason {
+	case "":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonNone
+	case "completed":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonCompleted
+	case "not_planned":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonNotPlanned
+	case "duplicate":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonDuplicate
+	case "other":
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonOther
+	default:
+		opts.Reason = issues_model.CloseReasonUnknown
+	}
+	return opts
 }

A way to store and retrieve "closed" reasons for issues and PRs
### User Story

As a front-end developer, I want a way to store messages detailing issue and PR close reasons in the system so that I can create a display on the front end to show the reason why an issue or PR was closed, but there is no current way to store nor recover the reason behind their closing.

### User Scenario

For a front-end developer to implement the feature, there needs to be a clear way to send and receive information, as it would be ridiculous to expect the front end to directly communicate with the DB. A central function will be implemented along with supporting infrastructure (such as a predefined list and constraints) that the user will need to implement the desired features.

The finer details on _how_ the information is stored by the system is abstracted away, and so, this single set of functionality will permit each storage and retrieval of the issue messages. This will similarly be the user story of how the API will handle the messages.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a database with existing open and closed issues and PRs, when the migration runs, then the close-reason columns exist on the issue table and every existing issue and PR has an empty reason; existing close comments, which have no close-reason metadata, also read as having no reason.
- [ ] AC2: Given an open issue, when it is closed through the close service with a valid reason (completed, not planned, duplicate or other), then both the issue and its new close timeline comment store that reason.
- [ ] AC3: Given the reason "other", when the text is empty or longer than 255 characters, then the close is rejected with its own error and the issue stays open; valid text is stored exactly as entered.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reason "duplicate", when the target number does not exist in the same repository or is the issue itself, then the close is rejected with its own error; a valid target is stored, and the close comment has the target issue loaded (number, title, link).
- [ ] AC5: Given a pull request, when it is closed as "completed", then the close is rejected with its own error; the allowed-reasons list for a PR leaves out "completed" and an issue's list includes all four.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue closed with a reason, when it is reopened, then the issue's reason is cleared and the earlier close comment keeps its reason.
- [ ] AC7: Given any existing close path (web, bulk, commit keyword, merged PR, branch deletion, API), when it closes an issue without a reason, then the close succeeds as before with an empty reason, and merging a PR still records no reason.



### Out of Scope

UI Displaying of information: Issue (#54 )
API access: Issue (#55 )
Issues for automatic closing of issues and PRs: Issue (#55 )

Other: Note that the pop ups on the UI will not show the reason since the message won't be written to the appropriate JSON field, for now. This will be addressed in the future (issue #55) to avoid touching the API under this issue.

### Open Questions

None

### Design Decisions
See below


### Scope

medium

				err = pull.LoadIssue(ctx)
				if err != nil {
					ctx.ServerError("load the issue of pull request error", err)

		} else if form.Status == "reopen" && issue.IsClosed && branchOtherUnmergedPR == nil {
			if err := issue_service.ReopenIssue(ctx, issue, ctx.Doer, ""); err != nil {
				log.Error("ReopenIssue: %v", err)
				ctx.Flash.Error("Unable to reopen.")
			}
		}
	} // end if: handle close or reopen

	ctx.JSONRedirect(redirect)
}
